header: 2.Scope and Limitations of this Technical Report

images.caption:
Figure 1.Overview ofAntom 3-in-1 Transformer.
(a)Sequence modality.Independent Transformer towers encode user, card, and device histories.
(b)Tabular modality.Field attention captures interactions among transaction attributes and business features.
(c)Graph modality.A graph attention network combines account profiles and rolling user
graphs to learn relational representations.
(d)Task-conditioned fusion.Task queries and sparse experts fuse sequence and tabular representations;
graph embeddings augment the risk head.Sequence, tabular, and graph encoders feed task-conditioned attention and sparse experts; pretraining objectives learn behavioral and relational representations.

Figure 2.Online scoring timeline of Antom 3-in-1 Transformer. Latencies are monitored values; braces mark service budgets. Stage widths are schematic.A horizontal time axis from the payment event to the risk decision, with the feature platform, the model service, and the strategy platform in sequence, their monitored latencies, and the 120 ms and 250 ms budgets.

Figure 3.Label efficiency on Antom-Merchant A and
Antom-Merchant B. Points and error bars show the
mean and standard deviation over three
fine-tuning runs.Four plots show AP and recall at a 0.5 percent intervention budget for the pretrained model and scratch training across five training-label budgets on AliExpress and ANTOM, with a dashed line for full-label scratch.

Figure 4.Pretrained representations of 2,880 annotated histories: PCA (left) and t-SNE (right).PCA and t-SNE projections of pretrained representations, with two behavior groups and an outlined t-SNE region used for case inspection.

Figure 5.Card and device switching after rejection, from the outlined region in Figure4.Three payment attempts show changes in anonymous card and device identities following rejections while retaining the IP identity, ending in a successful attempt.
